entries.description: This new guideline provides comprehensive clinical protocol organization with standardized content, with a Template which presents the format and structure of the protocol, including the table of contents, common headers, and contents; and a Technical Specification which presents the conformance, cardinality, and other technical attributes that enable the interoperable electronic exchange of protocol content.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice to stakeholders on implementing ICH M13B: Bioequivalence for immediate release solid oral dosage forms: Additional strengths biowaiver
entries.description: Part of the foreseen ICH M13 Guideline series (M13A-C), the ICH M13B Guideline is intended to provide recommendations on obtaining waivers of bioequivalence (BE) studies for one or more additional strengths of a drug product in an application where in vivo BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths. This guideline is applicable to both development and post approval phases for orally administered immediate-release (IR) solid oral dosage forms designed to deliver drugs to the systemic circulation, such as tablets, capsules, and granules/powders for oral suspension. The ICH M13B Guideline is the second Guideline in the foreseen series to describe the scientific and technical aspects of demonstrating BE for additional strengths of a drug product, i.e., obtaining waiver(s) for one or more strengths in an application with multiple strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths following ICH M13A. How regulatory decisions may be made based on BE assessment is out of the scope of this guideline.
entries.summary: Regulators now allow biowaivers for additional strengths of immediate‑release solid oral dosage forms when bioequivalence has been demonstrated for at least one strength.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling small molecule oral products must evaluate whether new strengths can be waived from in‑vivo studies, potentially reducing development timelines and costs.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: ICH guidelines implemented by Health Canada
entries.description: Health Canada has implemented and launched public consultations on several International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, reflecting Canada’s ongoing commitment to global regulatory harmonization. Stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines for consultation by the respective deadlines, as Health Canada will forward all comments to the ICH for consideration in the finalization process. Health Canada has begun implementing finalized guidelines. Stakeholders are encouraged to integrate these guidelines into their drug registration processes.
entries.summary: Health Canada is launching public consultations on several ICH guidelines to advance regulatory harmonization.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must review the draft guidelines and submit comments by the specified deadlines to ensure their drug registration processes align with forthcoming Canadian requirements.

entries.title: Qualifying notice for Calquence (302879)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada has issued a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Calquence, allowing its market authorization contingent on the sponsor conducting additional studies to confirm clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must plan and coordinate the required post‑market studies and ensure ongoing compliance, as the drug’s approval is conditional.

entries.label: WHO
entries.title: New WHO technical package to help countries improve health data for COVID-19 response and beyond
entries.description:
Today, as part of its commitment to strengthening health information systems and improving health[1], especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO announced a new approach to improving access to life-saving data: the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package. The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the urgent need for timely and reliable data to drive strategic health action. Too many countries still lack both the infrastructure to routinely gather health data and the analytical capacity to use these data for effective health actions and emergency response.

“Countries must be able to measure progress to make progress,” said WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “Particularly during COVID-19, reliable data is the best way to coordinate response efforts and improve health in all areas.”

Accurate health data are necessary to understand specific country needs in order to improve health and save lives. Data also helps direct scarce resources to where they are needed most.

The SCORE (Survey, Count, Optimize, Review, Enable) Technical Package aims to improve the availability of timely, reliable, validated, and comparable health data. For the first time in a single, harmonized package, it represents all the key elements for optimized health information system performance. Simply put, SCORE will help governments around the globe set benchmarks and i
entries.summary: WHO released the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package to improve health data availability and quality.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that this guidance may affect data reporting and health information systems within their organization.
